plan.query: Target-conditioned retrieval from category/brand/action/time histories when exact target-category matches are absent: DIN and DMR primary methods; field-context query construction, QueryFormer capacity-matched query replacements, and UniDot direct relevance readout controls.
plan.question: Why does target-aware history attention add little over pooling when the target category is absent from history, and can available field context recover useful cross-category or brand/action evidence? In the supplied single-seed validation receipts, AUC rises from 0.6050036145 (static) to 0.6102261137 (pooled) to 0.6133619861 (DIN). DIN minus pooled is 0.0026743907 for category-match-present histories (2,516,922 samples; 129,821 positives; 2,387,101 negatives), versus 0.0002617450 for category-match-absent histories (717,129 samples; 29,616 positives; 687,513 negatives). This is an exploratory difference in within-slice model gains, not proof of a query bottleneck or an interaction effect. Retrieve evidence to distinguish insufficient relevant input, weak query construction, and loss of explicit relevance signals before choosing a mechanism.
missing_information: Public candidate interface and baseline implementation: which static fields form the target query; how category, brand, action, time, masks, empty histories and pooling normalization are represented. No model files or ancestor sources are exposed in this phase.

Authorized primary DIN and DMR source text and precise method locators. Resolving the task-listed paper:din and paper:dmr references returned Unknown authorized reference; the retrieved cards do not substitute for inspecting these sources. No novelty or priority claim is verified.

Primary QueryFormer and UniDot methods and ablations at the card locators (queryformer-paper-v1 section 5.2 Table 4 and section 5.1; unidot-paper-v1 section 5.3 Table 4 and Appendix B Table 7), including query inputs, replacement capacity, compute, split policy and supervision. Cards are external reports, not evidence of local transfer.

Training-defined category/brand support and missingness; counts of target-brand matches conditional on target-category absence; per-action and recency distributions within the fixed 128-event causal prefix. Distinguish genuinely unavailable relevance from history truncation and unknown identifiers.

Paired prediction or authorized diagnostic access for user-cluster uncertainty on DIN-minus-pooled and its between-slice difference, plus intersections with history length, user training frequency, action composition and missing fields. Existing aggregate slices cannot isolate these explanations; empty histories also belong to the category-match-absent group.

Before any substantive experiment, record a prospective mechanism plan with inherited components and nearest-work differences, predicted and falsifying observations, alternative explanations, matched capacity and event-budget replacements, measured cost and final-assessment reserve. A possible diagnostic is to compare field-context queries against a capacity-matched target-only query while holding history and readout fixed; an explicit relevance readout needs a separate matched-head control. Their interaction would require factorial controls.

Paired seeds and measured end-to-end cost are required before treating a promising direction as supported. All three available trajectories succeeded; no failed or abandoned candidate trajectories are supplied, and no withheld outcomes are available or needed in this query phase.

cards.source_problem: Projection-only queries may insufficiently use field context when retrieving behavior evidence.
cards.reported_mechanism: Attention generates query probes; a field-sequence bridge refines evidence, while packed shared-parameter execution supports multiple views.

reported_evidence.summary: The paper compares query-generation replacements and view scaling. Its development split is not adopted for this task.
reported_evidence.locator: queryformer-paper-v1, section 5.2 Table 4; source split in section 5.1
limitations: The source uses a row-group holdout.
Component removal changes capacity and computation; nearest equal-budget replacement remains necessary.

conditions: target-aware history retrieval is useful on the available fields

transfer_risks: category/brand matching may need less expressive queries
multiple views can increase capacity without validating the query explanation
source task and development distribution differ
possible_discriminating_checks: replace query construction with a capacity-matched projection
separate query quality from view count and shared execution savings

cards.source_problem: Repeated nonlinear mixing may dilute explicit low-order relevance signals.
cards.reported_mechanism: Parallel field-mixing and sequence-retrieval paths exchange state; an FM Highway sends per-layer dot-product interactions directly to the classifier.

reported_evidence.summary: Component removal is studied in tiny single-path random-holdout mode. Removing the highway hurts most; removing bus fusion improves AUC but worsens Logloss, leaving the fusion explanation unresolved.
reported_evidence.locator: unidot-paper-v1, section 5.3 Table 4 and Appendix B Table 7
limitations: Small-mode ablations do not establish identical full-scale effects.
The final recipe changes capacity, optimization and supervision together.

conditions: explicit current-ad versus history-field relevance is meaningful
a deep model loses useful direct interaction information
missing_evidence: incremental value of direct interaction readouts
cost of sequence reuse across target queries

transfer_risks: conversion-delay supervision is unavailable in ordinary click labels
auxiliary heads and optimizer changes can confound architecture gains
a smaller shallow model may already preserve the relevant signals
possible_discriminating_checks: compare highway removal with a matched extra readout head
separate per-layer interactions, depth and training recipe
